keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; the 299-849 Maya envelope covers Palenque). The page gives only the site's area ('up to 2.5 km2' explored, 17.72 km2 national park, 1,772 ha UNESCO) and no kingdom extent or tributaries on the Usumacinta: 'Tributaries: page silent'. Drawn as a 20 km radius, the grid's minimum.

region.text: Palenque (Lakamha'), the seat of the B'aakal kingdom near the Usumacinta, Chiapas

ledger.note: 431: K'uk' Bahlam I founds the B'aakal dynasty at Palenque. He 'governed for four years starting in the year 431' (rulers table 431 to c. 435).

region.text: Palenque (Lakamha'), the seat of the B'aakal kingdom near the Usumacinta, Chiapas

ledger.note: 799: the last recorded ruler of Palenque. The rulers table lists Janaab Pakal III from 799 and the infobox gives 799 as the abandonment; 'there was no new elite construction in the ceremonial center sometime after 800' and a farming population stayed 'a few generations'.

wars.name: Calakmul's wars on Palenque
wars.outcome: 'Troops from Calakmul invaded and sacked Palenque' in 599 and again in 611 ('A second victory by Calakmul occurred some twelve years later, in 611'); no land is recorded as taken.
wars.note: The Calakmul page has Uneh Chan attacking on 23 April 599 'with his ally Lakam Chak' and sacking the city on 7 April 611.

wars.name: Toniná's sack of Palenque
wars.outcome: 'In 711, Palenque was sacked by the realm of Toniná' and the old king K'inich K'an Joy Chitam II was taken prisoner and presumably executed.
wars.note: The page names no land taken.

certainty.note: No frontier is recorded; the radius is the grid's minimum.

sources.title: Palenque
sources.note: B'aakal: 431 founding, Calakmul 599 and 611, Pakal 615-683, Toniná 711, 799 abandonment.

notes:
NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no Palenque row. The page opened gives no conquests with dates: the captures of 'the six enemy kings of the alliance' under Pakal (615-683) are undated, and Pomona, Tortuguero (659) and Santa Elena are 'page silent'. K'inich Janaab' Pakal (615-683) and K'inich Kan B'alam II (684-702) are the page's rulers; no ruler strip entered because the page's table was read only for 431 and 799.
NATIVE NAMES. B'aakal and Lakamha' are the page's own names (title of the section and the ancient name).
COUNTERPARTS. Toniná has no dossier (sacked Palenque in 711).
